newsitem.title: USA: Weekend rains soak dry areas of US Corn Belt - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Weekend rains soak dry areas of US Corn Belt - WSC.

text.p: Dry areas of the U.S. Corn Belt received much-needed rain over the weekend and further showers are forecast for this week, said David Taylor, senior agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
"It was a very good rain across the driest areas of the Corn Belt. The soybeans can still use it (the moisture) and it certainly won't harm the corn," he said.

Locations in central Illinois such as Decatur, Springfield and Quincy received 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain over the weekend while overall Illinois got 1.0 to 2.5 inches with 80 percent coverage. Only areas in the extreme south missed out.

There were also heavy showers in south-east Iowa where weekend totals ranged from 0.50 to 2.00 inches, in Indiana precipitation totalled 0.75 to 2.00 inches and in Ohio there were general rains of 1.00 to 3.00 inches.
WSC's Taylor noted another batch of showers were due to start moving across the U.S. Midwest late Tuesday

"Right now it (the rain) looks like it will not be as heavy, depending on how fast or slow it goes. Right now we are saying 0.25 to 1.00 inch with 50 to 70 percent coverage," Taylor said, noting these showers may help switch attention from dry crop conditions to cool temperatures.
"I don't think rain is a concern right now. The next concern will be cold weather," WSC's Taylor said.

He said temperatures this week in the north-east of the corn belt could fall as low as the upper 40s Fahrenheit and low 50s F. Temperatures were seen below normal across the corn belt at least for the next two or three days.
"The cool weather will prevent accumulation of growing degree days," he sid.
There were also showers over the weekend in North Dakota, where the spring wheat harvest is getting underway. Rain totals ranged from 0.30 to 1.00 inch.

More rain was forecast, possibly as early as late Monday, before the state starts to dry out late Tuesday through Thursday. Taylor noted, however, there could be more scattered showers in North Dakota on Friday and over the weekend.
